<objective>
Add TEE file enrollment to the desktop FUSE mount so that newly created files have their IPNS private keys wrapped with the TEE public key on first publish, enabling automatic 3-hour IPNS republishing by the TEE.

Purpose: Files created via the desktop app currently publish IPNS records without TEE enrollment (`encrypted_ipns_private_key: None`), meaning the TEE cannot republish their IPNS names. This makes file-level IPNS records go stale after 48 hours unless the user is online. The folder creation flow already has TEE enrollment (write_ops.rs:499-506); this plan replicates that pattern for per-file publishes.

Output: Modified `publish_file_metadata` on both Unix and Windows platforms that wraps the file IPNS key with the TEE public key on first publish.
</objective>

   253→//! Auto-update integration using tauri-plugin-updater.
   254→//!
   255→//! Checks for updates on launch (with 5-second delay), downloads in background,
   256→//! and notifies via system notification. Manual check available from tray menu.
   257→
   258→use tauri::AppHandle;
   259→use tauri_plugin_updater::UpdaterExt;
   260→
   261→/// Check for updates on app launch. Spawns async task with 5s delay.
   262→pub fn check_on_launch(app: &AppHandle) {
   263→    let handle = app.clone();
   264→    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
   265→        // Small delay to avoid competing with login/mount startup
   266→        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
   267→
   268→        if let Err(e) = do_update_check(&handle).await {
   269→            log::warn!("Update check failed: {}", e);
   270→        }
   271→    });
   272→}
   273→
   274→/// Manual check triggered from tray "Check for Updates..." menu item.
   275→pub fn manual_check(app: &AppHandle) {
   276→    let handle = app.clone();
   277→    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
   278→        match do_update_check(&handle).await {
   279→            Ok(found) => {
   280→                if !found {
   281→                    // No update available -- notify user since they asked explicitly
   282→                    use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   283→                    let _ = handle.notification()
   284→                        .builder()
   285→                        .title("CipherBox")
   286→                        .body("You are running the latest version.")
   287→                        .show();
   288→                }
   289→            }
   290→            Err(e) => {
   291→                use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   292→                let _ = handle.notification()
   293→                    .builder()
   294→                    .title("CipherBox")
   295→                    .body("Update check failed. Please try again later.")
   296→                    .show();
   297→                log::warn!("Manual update check failed: {}", e);
   298→            }
   299→        }
   300→    });
   301→}
   302→
   303→/// Perform the actual update check, download, and notification.
   304→/// Returns Ok(true) if an update was found and downloaded, Ok(false) if no update.
   305→async fn do_update_check(app: &AppHandle) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
   306→    let updater = app.updater()?;
   307→    let update = updater.check().await?;
   308→
   309→    if let Some(update) = update {
   310→        log::info!("Update available: v{}", update.version);
   311→
   312→        // Download and install (stages for next restart on macOS/Linux)
   313→        let version = update.version.clone();
   314→        update.download_and_install(
   315→            |chunk_length, content_length| {
   316→                log::debug!(
   317→                    "Downloading update: {} / {:?} bytes",
   318→                    chunk_length,
   319→                    content_length
   320→                );
   321→            },
   322→            || {
   323→                log::info!("Update downloaded, pending install on restart");
   324→            },
   325→        ).await?;
   326→
   327→        // Notify user via system notification
   328→        use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   329→        let _ = app.notification()
   330→            .builder()
   331→            .title("CipherBox Update Ready")
   332→            .body(&format!(
   333→                "CipherBox v{} is ready. It will be installed on next restart.",
   334→                version
   335→            ))
   336→            .show();
   337→
   338→        Ok(true)
   339→    } else {
   340→        log::info!("No update available (current version is latest)");
   341→        Ok(false)
   342→    }
   343→}
   344→```

```rust
//! Auto-update integration using tauri-plugin-updater.
//!
//! Checks for updates on launch (with 5-second delay), downloads in background,
//! and notifies via system notification. Manual check available from tray menu.

use tauri::AppHandle;
use tauri_plugin_updater::UpdaterExt;

/// Check for updates on app launch. Spawns async task with 5s delay.
pub fn check_on_launch(app: &AppHandle) {
    let handle = app.clone();
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
        // Small delay to avoid competing with login/mount startup
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;

        if let Err(e) = do_update_check(&handle).await {
            log::warn!("Update check failed: {}", e);
        }
    });
}

/// Manual check triggered from tray "Check for Updates..." menu item.
pub fn manual_check(app: &AppHandle) {
    let handle = app.clone();
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
        match do_update_check(&handle).await {
            Ok(found) => {
                if !found {
                    // No update available -- notify user since they asked explicitly
                    use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
                    let _ = handle.notification()
                        .builder()
                        .title("CipherBox")
                        .body("You are running the latest version.")
                        .show();
                }
            }
            Err(e) => {
                use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
                let _ = handle.notification()
                    .builder()
                    .title("CipherBox")
                    .body("Update check failed. Please try again later.")
                    .show();
                log::warn!("Manual update check failed: {}", e);
            }
        }
    });
}

/// Perform the actual update check, download, and notification.
/// Returns Ok(true) if an update was found and downloaded, Ok(false) if no update.
async fn do_update_check(app: &AppHandle) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let updater = app.updater()?;
    let update = updater.check().await?;

    if let Some(update) = update {
        log::info!("Update available: v{}", update.version);

        // Download and install (stages for next restart on macOS/Linux)
        let version = update.version.clone();
        update.download_and_install(
            |chunk_length, content_length| {
                log::debug!(
                    "Downloading update: {} / {:?} bytes",
                    chunk_length,
                    content_length
                );
            },
            || {
                log::info!("Update downloaded, pending install on restart");
            },
        ).await?;

        // Notify user via system notification
        use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
        let _ = app.notification()
            .builder()
            .title("CipherBox Update Ready")
            .body(&format!(
                "CipherBox v{} is ready. It will be installed on next restart.",
                version
            ))
            .show();

        Ok(true)
    } else {
        log::info!("No update available (current version is latest)");
        Ok(false)
    }
}
```

```yaml
name: Build Desktop

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: macos-latest
            args: '--target aarch64-apple-darwin'
            rust_target: 'aarch64-apple-darwin'
          - platform: macos-latest
            args: '--target x86_64-apple-darwin'
            rust_target: 'x86_64-apple-darwin'
          - platform: ubuntu-22.04
            args: ''
            rust_target: ''
          - platform: windows-latest
            args: '--no-default-features --features winfsp'
            rust_target: ''

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install Rust stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}

      - name: Rust cache
        uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: '. -> target'

      - name: Install Linux dependencies
        if: matrix.platform == 'ubuntu-22.04'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libappindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            patchelf \
            libfuse3-dev \
            fuse3

      - name: Install WinFsp (Windows)
        if: matrix.platform == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # Download and install WinFsp MSI (needed for winfsp crate build)
          $winfspUrl = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.0/winfsp-2.0.23075.msi"
          $winfspMsi = "$env:TEMP\winfsp.msi"
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $winfspUrl -OutFile $winfspMsi
          Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i", $winfspMsi, "/qn" -Wait

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: apps/desktop
        run: pnpm vite build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          releaseId: ${{ github.event.release.id }}
          updaterJsonPreferNsis: true
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          args: ${{ matrix.args }}
```

Key design decisions in this workflow:

2. **Matrix:** 4 builds -- macOS ARM64, macOS Intel, Ubuntu 22.04 (AppImage + deb), Windows (NSIS). Windows uses `--no-default-features --features winfsp` to build with WinFsp instead of FUSE.

3. **WinFsp install:** Windows build needs WinFsp SDK for the winfsp crate to compile. Download the MSI from GitHub releases and install silently.

4. **Frontend build:** Run `pnpm vite build` explicitly before tauri-action. The `beforeBuildCommand` in tauri.conf.json also does this, but running it separately gives clearer CI output.

5. **`updaterJsonPreferNsis: true`:** On Windows, prefer NSIS installer format in the updater manifest. This is the correct Windows format.

6. **`projectPath: apps/desktop`:** Since the desktop app is in a subdirectory of the monorepo, point tauri-action to it.

7. **Ed25519 signing:** `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` are read from GitHub Secrets at build time. If not set, updater artifacts will NOT have `.sig` files (builds succeed but updates cannot be verified).

8. **`releaseId`:** Attaches artifacts to the existing Release Please release instead of creating a new one. This means updater `latest.json` download URLs point to the same release.

   253→//! Auto-update integration using tauri-plugin-updater.
   254→//!
   255→//! Checks for updates on launch (with 5-second delay), downloads in background,
   256→//! and notifies via system notification. Manual check available from tray menu.
   257→
   258→use tauri::AppHandle;
   259→use tauri_plugin_updater::UpdaterExt;
   260→
   261→/// Check for updates on app launch. Spawns async task with 5s delay.
   262→pub fn check_on_launch(app: &AppHandle) {
   263→    let handle = app.clone();
   264→    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
   265→        // Small delay to avoid competing with login/mount startup
   266→        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
   267→
   268→        if let Err(e) = do_update_check(&handle).await {
   269→            log::warn!("Update check failed: {}", e);
   270→        }
   271→    });
   272→}
   273→
   274→/// Manual check triggered from tray "Check for Updates..." menu item.
   275→pub fn manual_check(app: &AppHandle) {
   276→    let handle = app.clone();
   277→    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
   278→        match do_update_check(&handle).await {
   279→            Ok(found) => {
   280→                if !found {
   281→                    // No update available -- notify user since they asked explicitly
   282→                    use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   283→                    let _ = handle.notification()
   284→                        .builder()
   285→                        .title("CipherBox")
   286→                        .body("You are running the latest version.")
   287→                        .show();
   288→                }
   289→            }
   290→            Err(e) => {
   291→                use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   292→                let _ = handle.notification()
   293→                    .builder()
   294→                    .title("CipherBox")
   295→                    .body("Update check failed. Please try again later.")
   296→                    .show();
   297→                log::warn!("Manual update check failed: {}", e);
   298→            }
   299→        }
   300→    });
   301→}
   302→
   303→/// Perform the actual update check, download, and notification.
   304→/// Returns Ok(true) if an update was found and downloaded, Ok(false) if no update.
   305→async fn do_update_check(app: &AppHandle) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
   306→    let updater = app.updater()?;
   307→    let update = updater.check().await?;
   308→
   309→    if let Some(update) = update {
   310→        log::info!("Update available: v{}", update.version);
   311→
   312→        // Download and install (stages for next restart on macOS/Linux)
   313→        let version = update.version.clone();
   314→        update.download_and_install(
   315→            |chunk_length, content_length| {
   316→                log::debug!(
   317→                    "Downloading update: {} / {:?} bytes",
   318→                    chunk_length,
   319→                    content_length
   320→                );
   321→            },
   322→            || {
   323→                log::info!("Update downloaded, pending install on restart");
   324→            },
   325→        ).await?;
   326→
   327→        // Notify user via system notification
   328→        use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   329→        let _ = app.notification()
   330→            .builder()
   331→            .title("CipherBox Update Ready")
   332→            .body(&format!(
   333→                "CipherBox v{} is ready. It will be installed on next restart.",
   334→                version
   335→            ))
   336→            .show();
   337→
   338→        Ok(true)
   339→    } else {
   340→        log::info!("No update available (current version is latest)");
   341→        Ok(false)
   342→    }
   343→}

   152→name: Build Desktop
   153→
   154→on:
   155→  release:
   156→    types: [published]
   157→
   158→permissions:
   159→  contents: write
   160→
   161→jobs:
   162→  build:
   163→    strategy:
   164→      fail-fast: false
   165→      matrix:
   166→        include:
   167→          - platform: macos-latest
   168→            args: '--target aarch64-apple-darwin'
   169→            rust_target: 'aarch64-apple-darwin'
   170→          - platform: macos-latest
   171→            args: '--target x86_64-apple-darwin'
   172→            rust_target: 'x86_64-apple-darwin'
   173→          - platform: ubuntu-22.04
   174→            args: ''
   175→            rust_target: ''
   176→          - platform: windows-latest
   177→            args: '--no-default-features --features winfsp'
   178→            rust_target: ''
   179→
   180→    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform }}
   181→    steps:
   182→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
   183→
   184→      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
   185→        with:
   186→          version: 10
   187→
   188→      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
   189→        with:
   190→          node-version: 20
   191→          cache: pnpm
   192→
   193→      - name: Install Rust stable
   194→        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
   195→        with:
   196→          targets: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
   197→
   198→      - name: Rust cache
   199→        uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
   200→        with:
   201→          workspaces: '. -> target'
   202→
   203→      - name: Install Linux dependencies
   204→        if: matrix.platform == 'ubuntu-22.04'
   205→        run: |
   206→          sudo apt-get update
   207→          sudo apt-get install -y \
   208→            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
   209→            libappindicator3-dev \
   210→            librsvg2-dev \
   211→            patchelf \
   212→            libfuse3-dev \
   213→            fuse3
   214→
   215→      - name: Install WinFsp (Windows)
   216→        if: matrix.platform == 'windows-latest'
   217→        shell: pwsh
   218→        run: |
   219→          # Download and install WinFsp MSI (needed for winfsp crate build)
   220→          $winfspUrl = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.0/winfsp-2.0.23075.msi"
   221→          $winfspMsi = "$env:TEMP\winfsp.msi"
   222→          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $winfspUrl -OutFile $winfspMsi
   223→          Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i", $winfspMsi, "/qn" -Wait
   224→
   225→      - name: Install dependencies
   226→        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
   227→
   228→      - name: Build frontend
   229→        working-directory: apps/desktop
   230→        run: pnpm vite build
   231→
   232→      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v1
   233→        env:
   234→          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   235→          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
   236→          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
   237→        with:
   238→          projectPath: apps/desktop
   239→          releaseId: ${{ github.event.release.id }}
   240→          updaterJsonPreferNsis: true
   241→          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
   242→          args: ${{ matrix.args }}
   243→```
   244→
   245→Key design decisions in this workflow:
   246→
   247→1. **Trigger:** `release: types: [published]` -- fires when Release Please publishes a GitHub Release. The `github.event.release.id` provides the release to attach artifacts to.
   248→
   249→2. **Matrix:** 4 builds -- macOS ARM64, macOS Intel, Ubuntu 22.04 (AppImage + deb), Windows (NSIS). Windows uses `--no-default-features --features winfsp` to build with WinFsp instead of FUSE.
   250→
   251→3. **WinFsp install:** Windows build needs WinFsp SDK for the winfsp crate to compile. Download the MSI from GitHub releases and install silently.
   252→
   253→4. **Frontend build:** Run `pnpm vite build` explicitly before tauri-action. The `beforeBuildCommand` in tauri.conf.json also does this, but running it separately gives clearer CI output.
   254→
   255→5. **`updaterJsonPreferNsis: true`:** On Windows, prefer NSIS installer format in the updater manifest. This is the correct Windows format.
   256→
   257→6. **`projectPath: apps/desktop`:** Since the desktop app is in a subdirectory of the monorepo, point tauri-action to it.
   258→
   259→7. **Ed25519 signing:** `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` are read from GitHub Secrets at build time. If not set, updater artifacts will NOT have `.sig` files (builds succeed but updates cannot be verified).
   260→
   261→8. **`releaseId`:** Attaches artifacts to the existing Release Please release instead of creating a new one. This means updater `latest.json` download URLs point to the same release.

Both are well-understood patterns with clear integration points in the existing codebase.

    11→The auto-update feature uses `tauri-plugin-updater` (v2.10.0), which provides Ed25519 (Minisign) signature verification, a `latest.json` manifest hosted on GitHub Releases, and a Rust API for checking/downloading/installing updates. The existing Release Please infrastructure creates GitHub Releases on every merge to main; the new CI job attaches signed desktop bundles and the updater manifest JSON to these releases.

    14→

   104→## Architecture Patterns
   105→
   106→### Recommended Project Structure
   107→
   108→```

   129→
   130→### Pattern 1: Tauri Updater Plugin Setup
   131→
   132→**What:** Register the updater plugin, configure `tauri.conf.json`, and check for updates on app launch.
   133→
   134→**When to use:** App startup.
   135→
   136→**Configuration (`tauri.conf.json`):**
   137→```json
   138→{
   139→  "bundle": {
   140→    "createUpdaterArtifacts": true
   141→  },
   142→  "plugins": {
   143→    "updater": {
   144→      "pubkey": "<MINISIGN_ED25519_PUBLIC_KEY>",
   145→      "endpoints": [
   146→        "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest/download/latest.json"
   147→      ]
   148→    }
   149→  }
   150→}
   151→```
   152→
   153→**Rust plugin registration (`main.rs`):**
   154→```rust
   155→// In tauri::Builder::default() chain:
   156→.plugin(tauri_plugin_updater::Builder::new().build())
   157→```
   158→
   159→**On-launch check (`updater.rs`):**
   160→```rust
   161→use tauri_plugin_updater::UpdaterExt;
   162→
   163→pub async fn check_for_update(app: &tauri::AppHandle) {
   164→    match app.updater().and_then(|u| Ok(u)) {
   165→        Ok(updater) => {
   166→            match updater.check().await {
   167→                Ok(Some(update)) => {
   168→                    log::info!("Update available: v{}", update.version);
   169→                    // Download in background
   170→                    match update.download_and_install(
   171→                        |chunk_len, content_len| { /* progress tracking */ },
   172→                        || { log::info!("Download complete, pending restart"); }
   173→                    ).await {
   174→                        Ok(()) => {
   175→                            // Notify user via tray
   176→                            send_update_notification(app, &update.version);
   177→                        }
   178→                        Err(e) => log::warn!("Update download failed: {}", e),
   179→                    }
   180→                }
   181→                Ok(None) => log::info!("No update available"),
   182→                Err(e) => log::warn!("Update check failed: {}", e),
   183→            }
   184→        }
   185→        Err(e) => log::warn!("Updater not available: {}", e),
   186→    }
   187→}
   188→```
   189→
   190→**Capability permissions (`default.json`):**
   191→```json
   192→"updater:default"
   193→```

   195→### Pattern 2: TEE File Enrollment on First Publish
   196→
   197→**What:** Wrap the file's IPNS private key with the TEE public key during the first per-file IPNS publish.
   198→
   199→**When to use:** When `publish_file_metadata` is called for a newly created file.
   200→
   201→**Existing folder enrollment pattern (`write_ops.rs:499-506`):**
   202→```rust
   203→let encrypted_ipns_for_tee = if let Some(ref tee_key) = fs.tee_public_key {
   204→    let wrapped = cipherbox_crypto::wrap_key(&ipns_private_key, tee_key)
   205→        .map_err(|e| format!("TEE key wrapping failed: {}", e))?;
   206→    Some(hex::encode(&wrapped))
   207→} else {
   208→    None
   209→};
   210→let tee_key_epoch = fs.tee_key_epoch;
   211→```
   212→
   213→**Required change in `publish_file_metadata` (`operations.rs:125`):**
   214→Add `tee_public_key: Option<&[u8]>` and `tee_key_epoch: Option<u32>` parameters, then:
   215→```rust
   216→let encrypted_ipns_for_tee = if let Some(tee_key) = tee_public_key {
   217→    let wrapped = cipherbox_crypto::wrap_key(file_ipns_private_key.as_slice(), tee_key)
   218→        .map_err(|e| format!("TEE key wrapping failed: {}", e))?;
   219→    Some(hex::encode(&wrapped))
   220→} else {
   221→    None
   222→};
   223→
   224→let req = cipherbox_api_client::IpnsPublishRequest {
   225→    // ... existing fields ...
   226→    encrypted_ipns_private_key: encrypted_ipns_for_tee,
   227→    key_epoch: tee_key_epoch,
   228→    // ...
   229→};
   230→```
   231→
   232→### Pattern 3: CI Desktop Build with tauri-action
   233→
   234→**What:** GitHub Actions workflow that builds desktop bundles for all platforms, signs with Ed25519, and uploads to GitHub Release.
   235→
   236→**When to use:** Triggered by Release Please creating a GitHub Release.
   237→
   238→**Workflow trigger approach:** The existing `release-please.yml` creates releases. A new `build-desktop.yml` workflow triggers on `release` events or is called by release-please with a `releaseId` to attach artifacts to the existing release.
   239→
   240→**tauri-action configuration:**
   241→```yaml
   242→- uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v1
   243→  env:
   244→    GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   245→    TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
   246→    TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
   247→  with:
   248→    releaseId: ${{ needs.release.outputs.release_id }}
   249→    uploadUpdaterJson: true
   250→```
   251→
   252→### Pattern 4: Install-on-Restart with Clean FUSE Unmount
   253→
   254→**What:** When the user quits the app (via tray "Quit CipherBox"), unmount FUSE cleanly before allowing the update to install.
   255→
   256→**When to use:** On quit when an update is pending.
   257→
   258→**Existing quit handler (`tray/mod.rs:272-279`):**
   259→```rust
   260→"quit" => {
   261→    #[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
   262→    {
   263→        let _ = crate::fuse::unmount_filesystem();
   264→    }
   265→    app.exit(0);
   266→}
   267→```
   268→
   269→The updater plugin handles restart automatically via `app.restart()`. The quit flow should:
   270→1. Drain pending uploads (wait for upload_tx queue to empty)
   271→2. Unmount FUSE
   272→3. Call `app.restart()` which triggers the pending update install
   273→
   274→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   275→
   276→- **Checking for updates from JavaScript:** The Rust API is more appropriate since the desktop app runs as a menu-bar utility without a visible window. Use `UpdaterExt` from Rust, not the JS `check()` function.
   277→- **Polling for updates:** Decision is launch-only check. Do NOT add a timer/interval.
   278→- **TEE enrollment on every publish:** Only enroll on FIRST publish (sequence 0 or first time for that IPNS name). Subsequent publishes for the same file should pass `None` since the TEE already has the key.
   279→- **Blocking FUSE thread for TEE wrapping:** The `wrap_key` call happens in the background upload thread (spawned in `release()`), NOT on the FUSE callback thread. This is already the correct pattern.
   280→
   281→## Don't Hand-Roll
   282→
   283→| Problem                | Don't Build                    | Use Instead                    | Why                                                   |
   284→| ---------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
   285→| Update verification    | Custom signature checking      | tauri-plugin-updater Ed25519   | Minisign is proven, handles edge cases                |
   286→| Update manifest        | Custom JSON format             | Tauri's `latest.json` format   | Standardized, tauri-action generates it automatically |
   287→| Update hosting         | Custom CDN/S3 upload           | GitHub Releases + tauri-action | Already have Release Please, zero additional infra    |
   288→| Key wrapping           | Custom ECIES implementation    | `cipherbox_crypto::wrap_key`   | Already used everywhere, tested                       |
   289→| Bundle signing in CI   | Manual openssl/minisign steps  | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` env | tauri-action reads it automatically                  |
   290→
   291→**Key insight:** Both features are integration work, not novel implementations. The updater uses a mature plugin with a well-defined protocol. The TEE enrollment reuses an existing pattern verbatim.
   292→
   293→## Common Pitfalls
   294→
   295→### Pitfall 1: Updater Endpoint URL Must Use GitHub's /latest/download/ Path
   296→
   297→**What goes wrong:** Using a direct release URL (e.g., `/releases/tag/v1.0.0/latest.json`) breaks because the updater checks the "latest" release dynamically.
   298→**Why it happens:** GitHub's `/releases/latest/download/` is a special redirect that always serves the latest release's assets.
   299→**How to avoid:** Use exactly: `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest/download/latest.json`
   300→**Warning signs:** 404 errors on update check, "no update available" when there should be one.
   301→
   302→### Pitfall 2: TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY Must Be Set at Build Time
   303→
   304→**What goes wrong:** Build succeeds but no `.sig` files are generated, making updates unverifiable.
   305→**Why it happens:** Tauri only generates updater signatures when `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` is set as an environment variable during `tauri build`. It does NOT read from `.env` files.
   306→**How to avoid:** Set as GitHub Actions secret, expose via `env:` in the workflow step.
   307→**Warning signs:** No `.sig` files in the build output, `latest.json` generated without signature fields.
   308→
   309→### Pitfall 3: createUpdaterArtifacts Must Be "true" in bundle Config
   310→
   311→**What goes wrong:** Build produces normal installers but no updater bundles (`.tar.gz` on macOS, `.AppImage` on Linux).
   312→**Why it happens:** Without `createUpdaterArtifacts`, Tauri doesn't generate the special updater format.
   313→**How to avoid:** Add `"createUpdaterArtifacts": true` to `bundle` section of `tauri.conf.json`.
   314→**Warning signs:** Missing `.tar.gz` for macOS, missing signatures.
   315→
   316→### Pitfall 4: Release Please Tag Format vs Updater latest.json
   317→
   318→**What goes wrong:** The updater's `latest.json` contains a version (e.g., `0.29.0`) but Release Please creates tags with a prefix (e.g., `cipher-box-v0.29.0`).
   319→**Why it happens:** The updater compares semver versions, while GitHub Releases uses tag names. The `latest.json` URLs must point to the actual release assets.
   320→**How to avoid:** Use `tauri-action`'s `releaseId` input to attach to the existing Release Please release rather than creating a new one. The action generates `latest.json` with correct download URLs.
   321→**Warning signs:** Version mismatch, 404 on download URLs.
   322→
   323→### Pitfall 5: TEE Enrollment Must Be Idempotent on the Server
   324→
   325→**What goes wrong:** Sending `encryptedIpnsPrivateKey` on a subsequent publish (not first) could overwrite the TEE's stored key or cause errors.
   326→**Why it happens:** The server-side `folder-ipns.entity.ts` stores `encryptedIpnsPrivateKey` -- sending it again on a non-first publish is harmless (server upserts), but wastes bandwidth.
   327→**How to avoid:** Only include TEE fields on the first publish for a given file IPNS name (when sequence number is 0). On subsequent publishes, pass `None`.
   328→**Warning signs:** No functional error, but unnecessary ECIES wrapping on every file save.
   329→
   330→### Pitfall 6: Windows Update Behavior Differs
   331→
   332→**What goes wrong:** On Windows, `download_and_install` immediately exits the application to run the NSIS installer. There is no "install on next restart" option.
   333→**Why it happens:** Windows NSIS installers need exclusive file access; Tauri force-exits the app.
   334→**How to avoid:** On Windows, show a confirmation dialog before calling `download_and_install`. On macOS/Linux, the update can be applied on restart.
   335→**Warning signs:** App closes unexpectedly on Windows during update.

   382→### Updater Module Skeleton
   383→
   384→```rust
   385→// Source: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/updater.rs (new)
   386→use tauri::AppHandle;
   387→use tauri_plugin_updater::UpdaterExt;
   388→
   389→/// Check for updates on app launch. Downloads in background, notifies via tray.
   390→pub fn check_on_launch(app: &AppHandle) {
   391→    let handle = app.clone();
   392→    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
   393→        // Small delay to avoid competing with login/mount startup
   394→        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
   395→
   396→        if let Err(e) = do_update_check(&handle).await {
   397→            log::warn!("Update check failed: {}", e);
   398→        }
   399→    });
   400→}
   401→
   402→async fn do_update_check(app: &AppHandle) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
   403→    let updater = app.updater()?;
   404→    let update = updater.check().await?;
   405→
   406→    if let Some(update) = update {
   407→        log::info!("Update available: v{}", update.version);
   408→
   409→        update.download_and_install(
   410→            |chunk_length, content_length| {
   411→                log::debug!(
   412→                    "Downloading update: {} / {:?} bytes",
   413→                    chunk_length,
   414→                    content_length
   415→                );
   416→            },
   417→            || {
   418→                log::info!("Update downloaded, pending install on restart");
   419→            },
   420→        ).await?;
   421→
   422→        // Send tray notification
   423→        use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   424→        let _ = app.notification()
   425→            .builder()
   426→            .title("CipherBox Update Ready")
   427→            .body(&format!(
   428→                "CipherBox v{} is ready. It will be installed on next restart.",
   429→                update.version
   430→            ))
   431→            .show();
   432→    } else {
   433→        log::info!("No update available (current version is latest)");
   434→    }
   435→
   436→    Ok(())
   437→}
   438→
   439→/// Manual check triggered from tray menu.
   440→pub fn manual_check(app: &AppHandle) {
   441→    let handle = app.clone();
   442→    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
   443→        match do_update_check(&handle).await {
   444→            Ok(()) => {}
   445→            Err(e) => {
   446→                use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   447→                let _ = handle.notification()
   448→                    .builder()
   449→                    .title("CipherBox")
   450→                    .body("No update available or check failed.")
   451→                    .show();
   452→                log::warn!("Manual update check failed: {}", e);
   453→            }
   454→        }
   455→    });
   456→}

   514→## State of the Art
   515→
   516→| Old Approach               | Current Approach                      | When Changed     | Impact                                   |
   517→| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
   518→| Tauri v1 built-in updater  | tauri-plugin-updater v2 (separate)    | Tauri v2 (2024)  | Plugin system, more flexible             |
   519→| `includeUpdaterJson`       | `uploadUpdaterJson` in tauri-action   | tauri-action v1  | Renamed parameter                        |
   520→| tauri-action@v0            | tauri-action@v1                       | 2025             | Stable release, better defaults          |
   521→| Manual `.sig` generation   | Automatic via `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Tauri v2     | Build-time signing, no manual steps      |
   522→| Custom update servers      | GitHub Releases `/latest/download/`   | Long-standing    | Zero infrastructure for open-source apps |
   523→
   524→**Deprecated/outdated:**
   525→
   526→- `tauri-action@v0`: Superseded by `v1`. Use `v1` for new projects.
   527→- `includeUpdaterJson`: Renamed to `uploadUpdaterJson` in tauri-action v1.
   528→- Tauri v1's built-in updater: Replaced by plugin architecture in v2.

   530→## Open Questions
   531→
   532→1. **Windows install-on-restart behavior**
   533→   - What we know: On Windows, `download_and_install` force-exits the app. On macOS/Linux, the update can be deferred.
   534→   - What's unclear: Whether Tauri v2.10 supports a "stage for next restart" mode on Windows, or if we need platform-specific logic.
   535→   - Recommendation: Test on Windows. If force-exit is unavoidable, show a confirmation prompt on Windows before applying. On macOS/Linux, stage silently and apply on next quit.
   536→
   537→2. **Release Please release ID propagation**
   538→   - What we know: tauri-action accepts a `releaseId` to attach artifacts to an existing release.
   539→   - What's unclear: How to extract the release ID from the Release Please workflow output.
   540→   - Recommendation: Use the `release` event trigger (fires when Release Please publishes), which provides `github.event.release.id` directly. Alternatively, query the GitHub API for the latest release.
   541→
   542→3. **Updater endpoint with `include-component-in-tag`**
   543→   - What we know: Release Please uses `include-component-in-tag: true`, creating tags like `cipher-box-v0.29.0`. GitHub's `/releases/latest/download/` serves the latest release regardless of tag format.
   544→   - What's unclear: Whether the updater correctly picks up releases tagged with a component prefix.
   545→   - Recommendation: The `/latest/download/` redirect works based on the "latest" release flag, not tag format. Verify in integration testing.

   206→      - name: Check for entity/migration drift
   207→        working-directory: apps/api
   208→        run: |
   209→          set +e
   210→          OUTPUT="$(pnpm typeorm migration:generate src/migrations/DriftCheck -d src/data-source.ts 2>&1)"
   211→          STATUS=$?
   212→          set -e
   213→
   214→          # Check if migration:generate failed before inspecting output files
   215→          if [ "$STATUS" -ne 0 ]; then
   216→            if echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "No changes in database schema were found"; then
   217→              echo "No entity/migration drift detected."
   218→              exit 0
   219→            fi
   220→            echo "::error::migration:generate failed unexpectedly."
   221→            echo "$OUTPUT"
   222→            exit 1
   223→          fi
   224→
   225→          if ls src/migrations/*DriftCheck*.ts 1>/dev/null 2>&1; then
   226→            # Our hand-written migrations use explicit constraint/index names, but TypeORM
   227→            # expects auto-generated hash-based names. Filter out cosmetic renames and only
   228→            # fail on real structural drift (new/dropped tables, added/removed columns, type changes).
   229→            if grep -qE 'CREATE TABLE|DROP TABLE|ADD COLUMN|DROP COLUMN|ALTER.*TYPE|RENAME COLUMN' src/migrations/*DriftCheck*.ts; then

   234→              echo ""

   236→              exit 1
   237→            else
   238→              echo "Only cosmetic constraint/index naming differences detected (not structural drift). OK."
   239→            fi
   240→          else
   241→            echo "No entity/migration drift detected."
   242→          fi

     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→Phase 25 adds two independent capabilities to the desktop app: (1) auto-update via the Tauri v2 built-in updater plugin backed by GitHub Releases, and (2) TEE enrollment for per-file IPNS keys created in the FUSE mount. Both are well-understood patterns with clear integration points in the existing codebase.
    10→
    11→The auto-update feature uses `tauri-plugin-updater` (v2.10.0), which provides Ed25519 (Minisign) signature verification, a `latest.json` manifest hosted on GitHub Releases, and a Rust API for checking/downloading/installing updates. The existing Release Please infrastructure creates GitHub Releases on every merge to main; the new CI job attaches signed desktop bundles and the updater manifest JSON to these releases.
    12→
    13→The TEE file enrollment is a surgical change: the existing `publish_file_metadata` function in `crates/fuse/src/operations.rs` already publishes per-file IPNS records but passes `encrypted_ipns_private_key: None`. The fix threads the TEE public key through this function and wraps the file's IPNS private key with it -- identical to the pattern already implemented for folder creation in `write_ops.rs:499-506` and in the web app's `file-metadata.service.ts:166-176`.
    14→
    15→**Primary recommendation:** Implement TEE file enrollment first (smaller change, clear pattern to follow), then the updater integration (larger CI/config change). Both are independent and can be done in any order.

   130→### Pattern 1: Tauri Updater Plugin Setup
   131→
   132→**What:** Register the updater plugin, configure `tauri.conf.json`, and check for updates on app launch.
   133→
   134→**When to use:** App startup.
   135→
   136→**Configuration (`tauri.conf.json`):**

   195→### Pattern 2: TEE File Enrollment on First Publish
   196→
   197→**What:** Wrap the file's IPNS private key with the TEE public key during the first per-file IPNS publish.

   252→### Pattern 4: Install-on-Restart with Clean FUSE Unmount
   253→
   254→**What:** When the user quits the app (via tray "Quit CipherBox"), unmount FUSE cleanly before allowing the update to install.
   255→
   256→**When to use:** On quit when an update is pending.
   257→
   258→**Existing quit handler (`tray/mod.rs:272-279`):**
   259→```rust
   260→"quit" => {
   261→    #[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
   262→    {
   263→        let _ = crate::fuse::unmount_filesystem();
   264→    }
   265→    app.exit(0);
   266→}
   267→```
   268→
   269→The updater plugin handles restart automatically via `app.restart()`. The quit flow should:
   270→1. Drain pending uploads (wait for upload_tx queue to empty)
   271→2. Unmount FUSE
   272→3. Call `app.restart()` which triggers the pending update install
   273→
   274→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   275→
   276→- **Checking for updates from JavaScript:** The Rust API is more appropriate since the desktop app runs as a menu-bar utility without a visible window. Use `UpdaterExt` from Rust, not the JS `check()` function.
   277→- **Polling for updates:** Decision is launch-only check. Do NOT add a timer/interval.
   278→- **TEE enrollment on every publish:** Only enroll on FIRST publish (sequence 0 or first time for that IPNS name). Subsequent publishes for the same file should pass `None` since the TEE already has the key.
   279→- **Blocking FUSE thread for TEE wrapping:** The `wrap_key` call happens in the background upload thread (spawned in `release()`), NOT on the FUSE callback thread. This is already the correct pattern.
   280→
   281→## Don't Hand-Roll
   282→
   283→| Problem                | Don't Build                    | Use Instead                    | Why                                                   |
   284→| ---------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
   285→| Update verification    | Custom signature checking      | tauri-plugin-updater Ed25519   | Minisign is proven, handles edge cases                |
   286→| Update manifest        | Custom JSON format             | Tauri's `latest.json` format   | Standardized, tauri-action generates it automatically |
   287→| Update hosting         | Custom CDN/S3 upload           | GitHub Releases + tauri-action | Already have Release Please, zero additional infra    |
   288→| Key wrapping           | Custom ECIES implementation    | `cipherbox_crypto::wrap_key`   | Already used everywhere, tested                       |
   289→| Bundle signing in CI   | Manual openssl/minisign steps  | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` env | tauri-action reads it automatically                  |
   290→
   291→**Key insight:** Both features are integration work, not novel implementations. The updater uses a mature plugin with a well-defined protocol. The TEE enrollment reuses an existing pattern verbatim.
   292→
   293→## Common Pitfalls
   294→
   295→### Pitfall 1: Updater Endpoint URL Must Use GitHub's /latest/download/ Path
   296→
   297→**What goes wrong:** Using a direct release URL (e.g., `/releases/tag/v1.0.0/latest.json`) breaks because the updater checks the "latest" release dynamically.
   298→**Why it happens:** GitHub's `/releases/latest/download/` is a special redirect that always serves the latest release's assets.
   299→**How to avoid:** Use exactly: `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest/download/latest.json`
   300→**Warning signs:** 404 errors on update check, "no update available" when there should be one.
   301→
   302→### Pitfall 2: TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY Must Be Set at Build Time
   303→
   304→**What goes wrong:** Build succeeds but no `.sig` files are generated, making updates unverifiable.
   305→**Why it happens:** Tauri only generates updater signatures when `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` is set as an environment variable during `tauri build`. It does NOT read from `.env` files.
   306→**How to avoid:** Set as GitHub Actions secret, expose via `env:` in the workflow step.
   307→**Warning signs:** No `.sig` files in the build output, `latest.json` generated without signature fields.
   308→
   309→### Pitfall 3: createUpdaterArtifacts Must Be "true" in bundle Config
   310→
   311→**What goes wrong:** Build produces normal installers but no updater bundles (`.tar.gz` on macOS, `.AppImage` on Linux).
   312→**Why it happens:** Without `createUpdaterArtifacts`, Tauri doesn't generate the special updater format.
   313→**How to avoid:** Add `"createUpdaterArtifacts": true` to `bundle` section of `tauri.conf.json`.
   314→**Warning signs:** Missing `.tar.gz` for macOS, missing signatures.
   315→
   316→### Pitfall 4: Release Please Tag Format vs Updater latest.json
   317→
   318→**What goes wrong:** The updater's `latest.json` contains a version (e.g., `0.29.0`) but Release Please creates tags with a prefix (e.g., `cipher-box-v0.29.0`).
   319→**Why it happens:** The updater compares semver versions, while GitHub Releases uses tag names. The `latest.json` URLs must point to the actual release assets.
   320→**How to avoid:** Use `tauri-action`'s `releaseId` input to attach to the existing Release Please release rather than creating a new one. The action generates `latest.json` with correct download URLs.
   321→**Warning signs:** Version mismatch, 404 on download URLs.
   322→
   323→### Pitfall 5: TEE Enrollment Must Be Idempotent on the Server
   324→
   325→**What goes wrong:** Sending `encryptedIpnsPrivateKey` on a subsequent publish (not first) could overwrite the TEE's stored key or cause errors.
   326→**Why it happens:** The server-side `folder-ipns.entity.ts` stores `encryptedIpnsPrivateKey` -- sending it again on a non-first publish is harmless (server upserts), but wastes bandwidth.
   327→**How to avoid:** Only include TEE fields on the first publish for a given file IPNS name (when sequence number is 0). On subsequent publishes, pass `None`.
   328→**Warning signs:** No functional error, but unnecessary ECIES wrapping on every file save.
   329→
   330→### Pitfall 6: Windows Update Behavior Differs
   331→
   332→**What goes wrong:** On Windows, `download_and_install` immediately exits the application to run the NSIS installer. There is no "install on next restart" option.
   333→**Why it happens:** Windows NSIS installers need exclusive file access; Tauri force-exits the app.
   334→**How to avoid:** On Windows, show a confirmation dialog before calling `download_and_install`. On macOS/Linux, the update can be applied on restart.
   335→**Warning signs:** App closes unexpectedly on Windows during update.

   382→### Updater Module Skeleton

   385→// Source: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/updater.rs (new)
   386→use tauri::AppHandle;
   387→use tauri_plugin_updater::UpdaterExt;
   388→
   389→/// Check for updates on app launch. Downloads in background, notifies via tray.
   390→pub fn check_on_launch(app: &AppHandle) {
   391→    let handle = app.clone();
   392→    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
   393→        // Small delay to avoid competing with login/mount startup
   394→        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
   395→
   396→        if let Err(e) = do_update_check(&handle).await {
   397→            log::warn!("Update check failed: {}", e);
   398→        }
   399→    });
   400→}
   401→
   402→async fn do_update_check(app: &AppHandle) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
   403→    let updater = app.updater()?;
   404→    let update = updater.check().await?;
   405→
   406→    if let Some(update) = update {
   407→        log::info!("Update available: v{}", update.version);
   408→
   409→        update.download_and_install(
   410→            |chunk_length, content_length| {
   411→                log::debug!(
   412→                    "Downloading update: {} / {:?} bytes",
   413→                    chunk_length,
   414→                    content_length
   415→                );
   416→            },
   417→            || {
   418→                log::info!("Update downloaded, pending install on restart");
   419→            },
   420→        ).await?;
   421→
   422→        // Send tray notification
   423→        use tauri_plugin_notification::NotificationExt;
   424→        let _ = app.notification()
   425→            .builder()
   426→            .title("CipherBox Update Ready")
   427→            .body(&format!(
   428→                "CipherBox v{} is ready. It will be installed on next restart.",
   429→                update.version
   430→            ))
   431→            .show();
   432→    } else {
   433→        log::info!("No update available (current version is latest)");

   514→## State of the Art

name: Build Desktop

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: macos-latest
            args: '--target aarch64-apple-darwin'
            rust_target: 'aarch64-apple-darwin'
          - platform: macos-latest
            args: '--target x86_64-apple-darwin'
            rust_target: 'x86_64-apple-darwin'
          - platform: ubuntu-22.04
            args: ''
            rust_target: ''
          - platform: windows-latest
            args: '--no-default-features --features winfsp'
            rust_target: ''

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install Rust stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}

      - name: Rust cache
        uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: '. -> target'

      - name: Install Linux dependencies
        if: matrix.platform == 'ubuntu-22.04'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libappindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            patchelf \
            libfuse3-dev \
            fuse3

      - name: Install FUSE-T (macOS)
        if: contains(matrix.platform, 'macos')
        run: |
          brew install --cask fuse-t
          sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig
          FUSE_T_PC="/Library/Application Support/fuse-t/pkgconfig/fuse-t.pc"
          if [ ! -f "$FUSE_T_PC" ]; then
            FUSE_T_PC=$(find /Library /usr/local /opt/homebrew -name "fuse-t.pc" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
          fi
          if [ -z "$FUSE_T_PC" ] || [ ! -f "$FUSE_T_PC" ]; then
            echo "::error::fuse-t.pc not found after FUSE-T installation"
            exit 1
          fi
          sudo cp "$FUSE_T_PC" /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc
          sudo sed -i '' 's/^Version:.*/Version: 2.9.9/' /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc

      - name: Install WinFsp (Windows)
        if: matrix.platform == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # Download and install WinFsp MSI (needed for winfsp crate build)
          $winfspUrl = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.0/winfsp-2.0.23075.msi"
          $winfspMsi = "$env:TEMP\winfsp.msi"
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $winfspUrl -OutFile $winfspMsi
          Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i", $winfspMsi, "/qn" -Wait

      - name: Create WinFsp MSI placeholder (Windows)
        if: matrix.platform == 'windows-latest'
        shell: pwsh
        run: New-Item -ItemType File -Force -Path "apps/desktop/src-tauri/resources/winfsp-placeholder.msi"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: apps/desktop
        run: pnpm vite build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          releaseId: ${{ github.event.release.id }}
          updaterJsonPreferNsis: true
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          args: ${{ matrix.args }}
